production.format_and_medium.summary: As an agency increases its use of electronic recordkeeping it must provide reasonable public access to records electronically maintained and must ensure exempt/confidential records are not disclosed except as permitted by law.

An agency must provide a copy of a record in the medium requested if it maintains the record in that medium; providing a copy in a medium not routinely used, or compiling/manipulating data, is charged under s. 119.07(4).

eligibility.any_person.summary: Every person has the right to inspect or copy any public record made or received in connection with the official business of any public body, officer, or employee of the state (or persons acting on their behalf), except records exempted under this section or made confidential by the Constitution.

eligibility.no_purpose_requirement.authority: Curry v. State, 811 So. 2d 736 (Fla. 4th DCA 2002); Lorei v. Smith, 464 So. 2d 1330 (Fla. 2d DCA 1985)
eligibility.no_purpose_requirement.summary: A custodian may not require the requester to state a reason or purpose for the request; the requester's motivation does not affect the right of access.

eligibility.no_residency_requirement.authority: Art. I, § 24(a), Fla. Const.; § 119.01(1), Fla. Stat.
eligibility.no_residency_requirement.summary: The right of access runs to 'every person' / 'any person' with no residency or citizenship qualification; a custodian may not condition access on the requester being a Florida resident.

custody.referral_to_proper_custodian.summary: A custodian may designate another officer or employee to permit inspection and copying, but must disclose the identity of the designee to the requester.

custody.contractor_and_thirdparty_custod.summary: A contractor providing services to a public agency must keep and maintain the public records required by the agency to perform the service.

On the agency custodian's request, a contractor must provide the agency a copy of, or allow inspection/copying of, requested records within a reasonable time at a cost not exceeding the chapter's fees.
custody.contractor_and_thirdparty_custod.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "within a reasonable time" from the agency custodian's request

custody.contractor_and_thirdparty_custod.summary: At contract completion the contractor must transfer, at no cost, all public records in its possession to the agency, or keep and maintain the records; if transferring, it must destroy exempt/confidential duplicates.

Many Florida cities charge actual cost for color — that practice would rest on (a)3.

media.label: Electronic media (CD/DVD/USB) charge
media.unit: actual cost of duplication of the medium (material and supplies — e.g., the disc/drive itself); no labor or overhead; special service charge only if IT use is 'extensive'
media.authority: § 119.07(4)(a)3., § 119.011(1), § 119.01(2)(f), Fla. Stat.; Fla. Att'y Gen., Government-in-the-Sunshine Manual (2024 ed., Vol. 46), Part II § G, p. 185 (AGO 13-03)
media.notes: CD/DVD/USB = 'all other copies' at actual cost of duplication (material and supplies). E-mail delivery: no identifiable duplication cost and no labor (AGO 13-03, City of Miami Gardens). Must supply in the medium requested if maintained in that medium.

delivery.label: Delivery: mail / handling / email / pickup
delivery.unit: mail: requester pays postage (actual cost); e-mail: no labor/overhead — only any actual cost of duplication; pickup/handling: no separate handling fee authorized
delivery.authority: Fla. Att'y Gen., Government-in-the-Sunshine Manual (2024 ed., Vol. 46), Part II § G, p. 185, 188 (Yanke v. State, 588 So. 2d 4 (Fla. 2d DCA 1991); AGO 13-03); § 119.011(1), Fla. Stat.
delivery.notes: No delivery fee schedule; postage at actual cost is the accepted practice per Yanke; e-mail effectively free (AGO 13-03).

certification.label: Certification / certified-copy charge
certification.notes: Ceiling under a Permission ('up to $1 per copy'); city sets the operative certification charge at or below $1.00, in addition to the duplication charge.

av.label: Audio/video: per recording, per minute, free minutes
av.unit: per recording: actual cost of duplication of the tape/disc (material and supplies); no per-minute rate; no free-minutes rule; special service charge only if 'extensive' IT/clerical work (e.g., voluminous redaction of recordings, with deposit permitted)
av.authority: § 119.07(4)(a)3., (d), § 119.011(1), Fla. Stat.; Fla. Att'y Gen., Government-in-the-Sunshine Manual (2024 ed., Vol. 46), Part II § G, p. 187, 189 (AGO 88-23; Morris Publishing Group v. State (1st DCA 2015))
av.notes: Audio/video copies are 'all other copies' at actual cost of duplication; a videotape or viewing machine is not an 'information technology resource' (AGO 88-23). Body-camera and other special-record fee provisions were not inventoried (out of scope).

commercial.label: Commercial-purpose schedule (surcharge %, labor becomes chargeable)
commercial.authority: Fla. Att'y Gen., Government-in-the-Sunshine Manual (2024 ed., Vol. 46), Part II § G, p. 164, 184 (Curry v. State (4th DCA 2002); Barfield (2d DCA 2014); AGO 85-03; AGO 84-03; AGO 76-34)
commercial.notes: A commercial-purpose surcharge or purpose-dependent labor rule has no footing under ch. 119: the requester need not state a purpose and only statutorily authorized fees may be imposed. Record-specific commercial-purpose statutes outside ch. 119 (e.g., DHSMV motor vehicle records) are not municipa…

waiver.label: Fee waiver: grounds, mandatory vs discretionary, purpose statement, written denial, appeal
waiver.value: discretionary; no statutory grounds; no purpose statement (purpose may not be required); no written-denial or appeal step
waiver.unit: enum_list: grounds=none in law; mandatory=false; purpose_statement=not permitted to require; written_denial=not required; appeal=none
waiver.authority: Fla. Att'y Gen., Government-in-the-Sunshine Manual (2024 ed., Vol. 46), Part II § G, p. 188 (AGO 90-81; Roesch v. State (Fla. 1993))
waiver.notes: Florida has no fee-waiver statute; an agency may choose to furnish copies free (AGO 90-81) but is not required to, even for indigent persons or inmates (Roesch).

waiver.forfeiture.label: Late response forfeits the fee
waiver.forfeiture.authority: ch. 119, Fla. Stat.; AG Manual 2024 ed. § G (searched)
waiver.forfeiture.notes: No late-response fee forfeiture in Florida law. The only forfeiture-like holding is Nader + Museu (fees not collectible where the agency skipped its own pre-production estimate/invoice policy) — recorded under rules.estimateNotifyThreshold, not a timing forfeiture. repeat.notes: No aggregation threshold or carry-forward rule for repeat requests; the only cross-request rule is the prior-unpaid-balance gate (payment.nonpayment). Searched: ch. 119 Fla. Stat. fee.copy_rate_per_page.summary: For duplicated copies of records not larger than 14 by 8.5 inches, the agency may charge up to 15 cents per one-sided copy.
For a two-sided copy, the agency may charge no more than an additional 5 cents.

fee.actual_cost_basis.summary: 'Actual cost of duplication' means the cost of the material and supplies used to duplicate the record, and does not include labor cost or overhead cost associated with such duplication.

fee.certified_copy_charge.summary: An agency may charge up to $1 per copy for a certified copy of a public record.

fee.nonstandard_rate.summary: For all copies other than standard-size paper copies, the agency charges the actual cost of duplication of the public record.
When a person photographs public records, the custodian may charge for supervision services at a rate agreed upon by the parties; if they cannot agree, the custodian determines the charge.
Where another room or place is necessary to photograph public records, the expense of providing it is paid by the person desiring to photograph the records.

fee.special_service_charge.summary: If the nature or volume of records requires extensive use of IT resources or extensive clerical/supervisory assistance, the agency may charge, in addition to actual duplication cost, a reasonable special service charge based on the cost actually incurred.

custody.custodian_definition_and_role.summary: Every person who has custody of a public record must permit that record to be inspected and copied by any person desiring to do so.
